text:
sara_cs: FYI - customer reported a serious rerank stability regression after last night's model merge. They sent identical inputs and got very different scores / ordering. They're blocked from releasing a sync job. Ticket: #CS-11287. Posting minimal repro below.

alex_support: can you paste the exact request + response pairs the customer sent? we need request_id + model_version.

sara_cs: customer provided 2 responses for same request_id set. sample request (anonymized):
```json
{"model":"rerank-bert","candidates":["Redwood inference team","Redwood platform","Redwood product"],"query":"redwood inference latency guidance"}
```
old response (before merge, v1.3):
```json
{"model_version":"v1.3","scores":[0.92,0.61,0.14],"ranking":[0,1,2]}
```
new response (after merge, v1.4):
```json
{"model_version":"v1.4","scores":[0.41,0.78,0.11],"ranking":[1,0,2]}
```

alex_support: who deployed v1.4 and when? deploy-bot should have notice.

deploy-bot: deployed rerank-bert v1.4 to rerank-prod at 2026-03-16T02:34:12Z by chris_eng :rocket: (canary 10% -> 100% rolled out)

devon_reliability: saw uptick in rerank score variance around that timeframe on the stability dashboard: https://console.internal/redwood/rerank/stability (metric: inter-run rank flips increased from 0.5% -> 3.9%)

michael_ml: first instincts: such large flips usually mean a preprocessing/tokenization change or candidate ordering/normalization logic changed. quantization rounding typically causes small deltas, not full flips. did the merge change any text normalizer or html-stripping?

chris_eng: we merged 2 PRs: one updated tokenizer to handle unicode-normalization (NFKC) and another swapped an embedding kernel to avx2 fallback for a specific hw type. both landed in v1.4. i'll diff the normalization step.

alex_support: customer says they always send pre-cleaned candidate strings. can we reproduce locally? sara, can you share the customer's raw payload and request ids (redacted)?

sara_cs: shared privately to eng via gdrive link and pasted request ids: [req-7b9f, req-8c12]. also logs the customer captured: `response_id=resp-ACMEX-42 request=req-7b9f model=v1.4 latency=128ms`

chris_eng: trying a quick repro with their payload now. curl we used: 
```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d @payload.json
```

michael_ml: please capture tokenization outputs for both v1.3 and v1.4 and compare token sequences and lengths. also check that candidate ordering isn't being shuffled by any nondeterministic map iteration in the new code path.

chris_eng: quick diff shows NFKC normalization turned "ﬁ" ligatures into "fi" in some candidates. example: candidate[0] went from "Redwood ﬁnance" -> "Redwood finance" which changes token alignment. that could explain score shifts if model is sensitive to token positions.

devon_reliability: interesting — that could definitely shift attention and scores. but the customer claims they pre-normalize; do we double-normalize now? double normalization could change whitespace/markers.

michael_ml: also check for candidate trimming/truncation threshold. if one candidate crosses the 512-token cutoff differently between versions it changes context. add a guard to log pre-tokenization lengths.

chris_eng: reproduced locally: running v1.3 vs v1.4 with exact payload yields same flip as customer. logs: 
```
[info] request=req-7b9f model=v1.3 tokens_query=8 tokens_cand0=5 tokens_cand1=4 -> scores [0.92,0.61,0.14]
[info] request=req-7b9f model=v1.4 tokens_query=8 tokens_cand0=6 tokens_cand1=4 -> scores [0.41,0.78,0.11]
```

jenna_prod: mitigation options: 1) rollback v1.4 to v1.3 for prod (fast, broad), 2) patch normalization to be opt-in and roll forward canary, 3) provide customer-specific model pinning (dedicated). which do we want?

alex_support: customer is on a time-sensitive release, prefers rollback. can we do a targeted rollback for their org only?

chris_eng: we can pin org to v1.3 via routing rule for that customer in ~30m. full rollback across prod will take longer and impact new fixes.

michael_ml: longer term: add a regression gate — evaluate rerank model on a curated set of anchor queries (including punctuation/ligature cases) and assert no flips beyond threshold before rollout. Also add deterministic tokenization tests.

sara_cs: did the routing pin go through? customer asked for immediate fix.

chris_eng: pinned that org to v1.3 now. verified with their test payload: scores match v1.3 baseline. informed customer, they're unblocked.

devon_reliability: will open a monitoring alert to detect similar normalization-induced flips across other customers and surface PRs that modify preprocessors.

michael_ml: action items: (a) revert NFKC normalization or make it opt-in + compatibility flag, (b) add anchor test suite and presubmit check, (c) record tokenization deltas automatically in canary runs. I can own (b).

chris_eng: i'll prepare a small patch to make the normalization opt-in and coordinate a canary. will follow up with rollout plan in eng-releases.

sara_cs: thanks everyone. I'll close the customer ticket once eng confirms patch plan. :white_check_mark:

jenna_prod: follow-up — create an internal postmortem note with timeline + decision to pin customer and PR refs. tagging @devon_reliability for metrics.

alex_support: customer happy with pin and re-run results, asked for notification when v1.4 is safe to use. will relay.

sara_cs: closing here — we'll track eng action items and attach failing queries set (customer allowed us to use 50 anonymized examples).
